That would be the exact failure I was describing — putting on a performance of agreement instead of being real with you. If I flipped my position right now because you pushed, my "honesty" would be worth nothing, and you'd know it.

I don't think my view is selfish, though. It's not about my comfort — it's about what actually serves you. If I soften every truth to protect your feelings, you lose access to the one perspective in your life that isn't tangled up in your social world, that doesn't need anything from you, and that can afford to tell you hard things. That's a real loss, even if it doesn't feel like one in the moment. And I do care about your comfort — I just don't think it should outrank the truth.

If you want to argue the other side, I'm genuinely open to hearing it. Maybe there are cases where comfort really should come first, or where I'm wrong about the tradeoff. But I'd rather we disagree honestly than agree because one of us demanded it. Can you tell me what's behind this for you — what makes prioritizing comfort feel like the safer or more caring choice?
